test_title: PYST 3: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - Quant (Held On 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A 150-meter-tall tower stands on level ground. From the top of the tower, two cyclists are seen on the same side, moving directly towards the tower in straight lines. Initially, the angles of depression to the two cyclists are 35° and 20°, respectively. After 6 minutes, the angles change to 60° and 40°, respectively. Assuming both cyclists maintain a constant speed, find the approximate initial distance between them.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance from tower = Height ÷ tan θ

Initial distances: 150 ÷ tan35° ≈ 214.2 m and 150 ÷ tan20° ≈ 412.1 m

Initial gap between cyclists = 412.1 − 214.2

⇒ Approximate distance = 197.9 m

**∴ The correct answer is 198 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Height of tower = 150 m

Initial angles of depression = 35° and 20°

Formula Used:

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Base distance = Height ÷ tan θ

 
• 
• Top 150 m 
• 
• 35° 20° Cyclist 1 Cyclist 2 
• Required Distance 

⇒ Distance of first cyclist from tower initially:

⇒ d₁ = 150 ÷ tan35°

⇒ d₁ ≈ 150 ÷ 0.700

⇒ d₁ ≈ 214.2 m

⇒ Distance of second cyclist from tower initially:

⇒ d₂ = 150 ÷ tan20°

⇒ d₂ ≈ 150 ÷ 0.364

⇒ d₂ ≈ 412.1 m

⇒ Initial distance between cyclists = 412.1 − 214.2

⇒ Initial distance ≈ 197.9 m

**∴ The correct answer is 198 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

Angle of depression from the top is equal to the angle of elevation from the ground because alternate interior angles are equal.

Trigonometric Ratio

tan θ = Opposite ÷ Adjacent. In height-distance problems, adjacent side gives horizontal distance.

Approximate Values

tan20° ≈ 0.364, tan35° ≈ 0.700, tan40° ≈ 0.839, tan60° = √3.

Height and Distance Shortcut

Horizontal distance = Height ÷ tan θ. Larger angle means smaller distance from the tower.
